evidence.summary: bitmidi 101826 whistle track 16 (program 78) events 0-25, a humanized single-voice performance at 75 BPM. The Musicnotes MN0072706 publisher preview (Universal/PolyGram 1990, vocal staff labelled "(Whistle)", image SHA-256 d83a892d4bb01ab9916cda441c4d4ada459143304b47806ee5242e28fd2ec9fd) bars 1-7 give the same 26 pitches (+24 octave convention) and attacks within 0.1 beat, plus a bar-7 B half note with no visible tie from the bar-6 B eighth. MIDI and the DPSM piano solo (MN0237111) keep one held B, so the single sustained B is retained and the extra score attack is a documented variant. midiworld 3604 is the same transcription family.

title: Eine kleine Nachtmusik

evidence.summary: Mutopia violin I MIDI track 0 (144 BPM). Bar 1 beat 1 is the triple stop D4-B4-G5 (events 0-2, Mutopia preview image shows the chord); viola and cello attack a single G at the same instant and all parts continue in unison with D5-G5-D5, so the melodic voice is the chord top G5 (event 2), chord tones D4/B4 excluded. Edition Peters piano four-hands Primo (Commons scan, PDF page 3) prints the same 18-note line with a single G5. Wikipedia revision 1373567689 "First theme" LilyPond agrees. bitmidi 35036 rolls the chord (G5 0.156 beat late).

title: El Chavo del Ocho
hook: Complete A section of the show theme (notation video bars 1-8)

evidence.summary: Direct transcription from a bounded frame (t = 10 s) of the Joyce Garcia notation video "Marcha Turca de las Ruinas de Atenas (El Chavo del ocho)" (2/4, A minor, no ornaments), frame SHA-256 e4034112ac04a1fa4e06fb4e94ceddd9a0365064a118d66811cdc12c5bfc5706. Its form (A twice-phrased with an E-F-G half cadence, then B strain and A return) is the show version derived from Jean-Jacques Perrey's "The Elephant Never Forgets" (1970); Beethoven's Op. 113 No. 4 violin I (IMSLP 20118) states only the four-bar phrase ending F-F#-G before its B strain and has acciaccature. bitmidi 8169 track 0 events 1-4, 6-18, 20-23 and 25-35 match all pitches and attacks; its four E acciaccature (events 0, 5, 19, 24) are ornaments absent from the primary. Tempo from the MIDI bar length.

title: Secret Discovered
hook: Complete A Link to the Past secret jingle: 8 sixteenths ending on the held (fermata) final note

evidence.summary: Direct transcription of Mikhail Hogrefe's "Found Secret" from The Legend of Zelda: A Link to the Past (accurate-video-game-sheet-music, commit 6d81f89), engraving PNG SHA-256 dc8f69e79194444d9a32933a67f3779fc586aba35821c19721e4c5498e725a0c, LilyPond source asserted: one 2/4 bar of eight sixteenths at quarter = 115 (Gb7 F7 D7 Ab6 G6 Eb7 G7 B7 sounding, 15ma), fermata on the last note, marked Echo. His MIDI rendering has the same pitches and attacks. BitMidi 101252 "The Legend of Zelda - Uncover Secret" track 0 events 0-7 (G5 F#5 D#5 A4 G#4 E5 G#5 C6, 120 BPM) agrees on all intervals after a constant +23 and on every attack within 0.023 beat. The same transcriber's Link's Awakening "Got Secret" equals the LA DX game-data decode exactly, supporting his pitch and rhythm method. No ALttP or OoT game data was decoded; the fermata hold length is not quantified by any source.
